name: Azariah
overview: Azariah was a male Levite who served as an Aaronic priest through the line of Eleazar. He is identified as the son of Ahimaaz and the father of Johanan, situating him within the priestly lineage recorded in 1 Chronicles 6:9. His role reflects the continuation of priestly duties within the tribe of Levi.
namesAndTitles: The name Azariah means 'YHWH has helped,' highlighting a recognition of divine assistance. This proper name is recorded in 1 Chronicles 6:9 and was not given directly by God, indicating its common use within the Hebrew tradition.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Azariah as the son of Ahimaaz and the father of Johanan, establishing a clear generational link within the Levitical priesthood. No other familial relationships are recorded beyond these in the provided data.
scriptureSignificance: Azariah's significance lies in his place within the Aaronic priestly line, emphasizing the faithfulness of the Levitical heritage through Eleazar. His familial connections underscore the transmission of priestly responsibilities, which were vital for maintaining the worship and holiness prescribed by God. While other individuals named Azariah appear in Scripture, this particular Azariah exemplifies the continuity of God's covenantal priesthood.
